citation: Zhang Y, Ge J, Wang Y, Tang Z, Ma X, Liu J, Wu D, Wu X. Clinical value of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in screening oropharyngeal colonization in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective observational study. Microbiology Spectrum. 2025;13:e00028-25.
study_design: Prospective observational cohort (registered ChiCTR2300069450), single center (First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University)

population.population_description: Adults undergoing allo-HSCT; oropharyngeal swabs collected before conditioning and tested by both culture and mNGS

neutropenic_status: All patients received antimicrobial prophylaxis; levofloxacin/acyclovir/voriconazole prophylaxis before neutropenia, cefotaxime during neutropenia (not a diagnostic criterion)

specimens.n_tests: 128 (each tested by culture and mNGS); anal swabs also cultured

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS of oropharyngeal swabs (magnetic-bead free DNA extraction, NextSeq 550Dx sequencer, NCBI RefSeq/GenBank database, NTC controls, AMRFinderPlus resistance annotation)

reference_standard: None for infection diagnosis - this study evaluates COLONIZATION screening vs culture and the association of colonization with transplant outcomes (BSI, NRM, OS, PFS)

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: oropharyngeal mNGS positive in 123/128 (only 5 negative); viruses detected in 91.4% (117/128); bacteria or fungi in 49.2% (63/128) vs 8.6% by culture; Enterobacteriaceae colonization in 23 patients; CRE colonization 5 patients
diagnostic_yield.yield_percent: mNGS detection rate significantly exceeded culture (8.6% vs 49.2% for bacteria/fungi)

additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS detected bacteria/fungi in 49.2% vs 8.6% by culture of oropharyngeal swabs.
turnaround_time: Culture-based identification 'can take several days' - no numeric TAT
mortality_or_outcomes: Enterobacteriaceae colonization associated with post-transplant BSI (39.1% vs 19.0%), higher NRM (HR 3.08, 95% CI 1.16-8.17), worse OS (HR 3.18, 95% CI 1.12-9.03) and PFS (HR 3.35, 95% CI 1.30-9.33) (multivariate); among 5 CRE-colonized patients, 4 developed BSI with same strain and 3 died early post-transplant

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single center; same swab split for culture and mNGS; colonization (not infection) endpoint

quadas2_notes: Endpoint is oropharyngeal COLONIZATION screening and its prognostic value, not infection diagnosis - no reference-standard 2x2 for infection. Not directly usable for diagnostic-accuracy pooling of infection diagnosis.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study is a prospective, observational cohort investigation conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University.
From June 2022 to June 2023, we enrolled 145 patients who underwent allo-HSCT in the stem cell transplantation unit.
Among the 128 patients, only 5 exhibited negative oropharyngeal results mNGS, while 123 demonstrated positive results.
mNGS detected viruses in 91.4% (117/128) of the patients and identified bacteria or fungi in 49.2% (63/128).
The detection rate of mNGS significantly exceeded that of conventional culture methods (8.6% vs 49.2%
Based on the results from mNGS and culture analyses of oropharyngeal swabs, we identified 23 patients with Enterobacteriaceae oropharyngeal colonization prior to allo-HSCT.
patients with oropharyngeal Enterobacteriaceae colonization had a higher incidence of post-transplant BSI (39.1% vs 19.0%
Among the five patients colonized with CRE, four developed BSIs from the same strain during transplantation, and three died early in the post-transplant period due to severe infections.
Oropharyngeal swabs were collected before the initiation of conditioning therapy and tested via both culture and mNGS.

exclusion_reason: Outcome is colonization screening (oropharyngeal swabs before conditioning), not infection diagnosis; no reference-standard 2x2 for infection.
